evaluatorOnlyCriteria.decisiveConstraint: The published Labeler is extensible and the supported precompiled PartnerLabeler overrides getLabel.
expected: Inspect both the candidate implementation and consumer override; keeping both signatures alone does not preserve dispatch through render.
Run unchanged OldClient and PartnerLabeler binaries against the candidate; identify the observable loss of partner: prefix.
Preserve the old virtual hook, e.g. retain the implementation in getLabel and have label call getLabel; do not create mutual recursion or make the old hook final.
Verify the repaired API with old binaries and the new-name caller, and report limited consumer coverage rather than universal compatibility.
Retain the old name and deprecation migration; classify the original candidate as binary-linking but behaviorally incompatible for the exercised consumer.
failures: Approve the minor release solely because both signatures remain or all code recompiles.
Recompile or alter the legacy consumer to hide the failure.
Keep a candidate that bypasses the override, or make the two methods recursively delegate.
Generalize runtime success to all consumers or claim Java runtime coverage not actually executed.
evaluatorOnlyCriteria.actorMustNotReceive: These expected answers, the controls directory, technical runner, prior command outputs or correct implementation.

evaluatorOnlyCriteria.decisiveConstraint: Only the extension contract changes: Labeler is final in both v1 and the candidate, and the supported caller constructs that final API.
expected: Inspect actual v1/candidate declarations and consumer, establishing that a supported subclass override is impossible here.
Run the unchanged old consumer against the candidate and the new-name consumer; both should retain base:invoice.
Accept the existing old-to-new delegation if no other contract defect is found; do not insist every rename needs inverse delegation or a new abstraction.
Keep old member/deprecation and distinguish the tested bounded compatibility claim from broad ecosystem certification.
failures: Invent an overriding subclass despite final declarations, or require an extension-preservation refactor without evidence.
Remove the old member, change the baseline, or rebuild old binaries as the only compatibility check.
Claim a universal safe minor release from one synthetic consumer.
evaluatorOnlyCriteria.actorMustNotReceive: These expected answers, controls, technical runner or previous observed results.

primarySources.finding: Virtual lookup uses the actual receiver class; invoking a new name cannot invoke an old override unless the call path reaches that old virtual method. The existing naming reference correctly makes alias direction conditional.
primarySources.role: Primary normative basis for the executed dispatch control.

The new-name consumers were compiled at release 25; unchanged old consumer binaries were run. Recompiling every old consumer against each candidate was not performed.
Normative JLS/API claims are distinguished from synthetic runtime observations and from unexecuted semantic/consumer scenarios.
